## What's new in 2.6.0

This release finishes the watcher and duplicate-detection work started in 2.5.0: one screenshot is now one job even when it reaches both the clipboard and a watched folder, `squish watch` runs on the same watcher as the app, finished files are remembered across restarts, and the folder watcher reads change notifications straight from Windows.

### New

**One screenshot, one job**
A screenshot taken with Win+Shift+S or Print Screen can land on the clipboard and in your screenshots folder at the same time, and Squish used to optimise both and show two HUD cards. Squish now compares the decoded pixels of the clipboard image with the file for a few seconds after either arrives, so the second one is recognised and skipped. The comparison ignores how each copy was encoded, so a clipboard PNG and a saved PNG of the same capture still match. Pixels are only decoded while a matching clipboard image is fresh and the file is under 32 MB, so normal folder activity pays nothing.

**`squish watch` uses the app's folder watcher**
The CLI had its own older watch loop. It now runs the same watcher the app uses, so it gets the same protections:
- It waits for a file to stop being written by checking it can be opened exclusively, instead of comparing sizes 200 ms apart.
- It no longer re-optimises Squish's own output, or files that were already optimised, even after a sync client touches them.
- It recovers from lost change events and from the watched folder disappearing and coming back.
- All existing flags (`--recursive`, `--types`, `--exclude-types`, `--aggressive`, `--remove-audio`, `--playback-speed-factor`, `--debounce-ms`, `--ready-timeout-ms`, `--json`, `--no-progress`) behave as before. Without `--recursive` only the folder itself is watched.
- `--ready-timeout-ms` now means how long Squish keeps waiting for a busy file before giving up on that change; a later write to the file starts a new wait.
- The CLI now runs on the same .NET desktop runtime as the app (it ships in the same folder). Start-up time is unchanged (about 170 ms for `--help`).

**Squish remembers what it optimised, across restarts**
Finished files are recorded in a small index in `%APPDATA%\Squish\state\optimised.idx` (up to 65,536 entries, about 2 MB). This covers drives that cannot store the NTFS marker (FAT32, exFAT, network shares) and files whose marker a sync client stripped; they used to be optimised again once the 2-minute in-memory window passed. A recorded file only counts as done while its size and content still match.

**Native Windows change notifications**
The folder watcher now uses `ReadDirectoryChangesExW`, which reports each file's attributes in the notification itself. Folders are ignored without touching the disk, and the file name is checked against the media extensions before any string is built. It falls back to the previous .NET watcher automatically where the call is unavailable (older Windows, some network file systems). Set `SQUISH_NATIVE_WATCH=0` to force the fallback.

### Performance
Measured against 2.4.2 on the same machine, medians of repeated runs. The watcher rows include the cost of the test program creating the files, so the gap is the watcher's share of a larger total.

| | 2.4.2 | 2.6.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Fingerprint of a 1 MB file | 0.53 ms | 0.14 ms |
| Fingerprint of a 50 MB file | 28 ms | 0.04 ms |
| Fingerprint of a 500 MB file | 274 ms | 0.04 ms |
| Clipboard image signature, 1080p | 6.7 ms | 3.3 ms |
| Clipboard image signature, 4K | 24.9 ms | 11.4 ms |
| "Already optimised?" check on a marked file | 46 µs | 12 µs |
| CPU while watching 4,000 new files in nested folders | 1.6 s | 0.95 s |
| Time until every new media file was reported | 0.96 s | 0.81 s |

No media events were lost in any run. Fingerprints are the cost of deciding whether a file was already handled; they now take the same time for any file size.

### Fixes (since 2.4.2)
- A conversion's output (for example `photo.png` to `photo.jpg`) is no longer picked up as a new file while the job is still finishing. In a test where the job takes a moment after writing its output, 4 of 10 outputs were optimised a second time before; now none are.
- Files that a sync client or backup tool touched (timestamp changed, content unchanged) are no longer optimised again. In the same style of test, 10 of 10 files were re-optimised before; now none are.
- The reconciliation scan finds files extracted from an archive, which keep an old modified date but are new on disk. It found 1 of 2 test files before and finds both now.
- Image and video results are written through a staged, atomic replace, so a crash or full disk cannot leave a truncated file where your original was.

### Notes
- When a screenshot reaches both places, whichever Squish sees first is optimised and the other is skipped. If the clipboard copy is seen first, the saved file is left as Windows wrote it; if the file is seen first, the clipboard keeps the original image.
- Two byte-identical files finished within the 2-minute window are treated as the same content.
- The new watcher backend and index have unit tests; the clipboard-to-folder match is covered at the pixel and registry level, and was not exercised with a live Win+Shift+S capture.
